stories.headline: SpaceX Files Confidentially for IPO Targeting $1.75T Valuation, Could Raise Over $50B

key_facts.fact: SpaceX has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering, setting the stage for what could become the largest stock market listing on record.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk's SpaceX has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday, setting the stage for what could become the largest stock market listing on record.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX could seek to raise more than $50 billion, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 record IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: The Starbase, Texas-headquartered firm could seek to raise more than $50 billion in the IPO, handily surpassing the 2019 flotation of Saudi Aramco, which remains the largest IPO on record.

key_facts.fact: The valuation of more than $1.75 trillion comes after SpaceX merged with Musk's AI startup xAI, which valued the rocket company at $1 trillion and xAI at $250 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: A public listing at a potential valuation of more than $1.75 trillion comes after SpaceX merged with Musk's artificial intelligence startup xAI in a deal that valued the rocket company at $1 trillion and the developer of the Grok chatbot at $250 billion.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX has selected five lead banks — Bank of America, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, and Morgan Stanley — with 21 banks total involved in the deal code-named 'Project Apex'.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX taps 21 banks for 'Project Apex' IPO, targets $1.75 trillion valuation

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is hosting an analyst day on April 21 and offering analysts an optional visit to xAI's 'Macrohard' data center in Memphis on April 23.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX is hosting an analyst day on April 21, encouraging research analysts to attend in person... The company is also offering analysts an optional visit to xAI's 'Macrohard' data center site in Memphis, Tennessee, on April 23.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX generated about $8 billion in profit on $15-16 billion in revenue last year, with Starlink having 9 million subscribers.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX generated about $8 billion in profit on $15 billion to $16 billion of revenue last year... 'Starlink is the only reason this valuation is defensible,' Boloor said. 'This is going to be the recurring revenue engine' with 9 million subscribers.

stories.headline: Intel Pays $14.2B to Buy Back Apollo's 49% Stake in Ireland Fab 34, Plans $6.5B in New Debt

key_facts.fact: Intel agreed to repurchase Apollo Global Management's 49% stake in the Fab 34 joint venture in Ireland for $14.2 billion, restoring full ownership.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel has reached an agreement to repurchase Apollo Global Management's 49% interest in its Fab 34 semiconductor manufacturing facility located in Ireland for $14.2 billion, restoring complete control of the operation.

key_facts.fact: Apollo originally purchased the 49% stake in 2024 for $11.2 billion, meaning it earned a $3 billion premium in roughly 18 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo initially purchased this stake during 2024 for $11.2 billion, providing Intel with critical capital during a period of significant financial strain.

key_facts.fact: Intel plans to finance the buyback through available cash and approximately $6.5 billion in new debt.
key_facts.excerpt: The semiconductor giant plans to finance this acquisition through a combination of available cash and approximately $6.5 billion in fresh borrowing.

key_facts.fact: Fab 34 in Leixlip, Ireland manufactures semiconductors using Intel 4 and Intel 3 process technologies and is Intel's first high-volume EUV lithography facility.
key_facts.excerpt: The Fab 34 facility is situated in Leixlip, on the outskirts of Dublin. The plant manufactures semiconductors utilizing Intel 4 and Intel 3 process technologies... Intel's inaugural high-volume production location to deploy extreme ultraviolet lithography equipment.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares closed up nearly 9% on the news.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Intel climbed 6% following Wednesday morning's announcement.

stories.headline: Chinese Chipmakers Capture 41% of China's AI Server Market as Nvidia's Share Erodes to 55%

key_facts.fact: Chinese GPU and AI chip makers captured nearly 41% of China's AI accelerator server market in 2025, shipping 1.65 million cards, according to IDC data reviewed by Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese GPU and AI chip makers captured nearly 41% of China's AI accelerator server market last year, eroding Nvidia's once-dominant position in one of its most important overseas markets, according to data from an IDC report reviewed by Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Total AI accelerator card shipments in China reached approximately 4 million units in 2025, with Nvidia shipping around 2.2 million cards for a 55% share.
key_facts.excerpt: Total shipments of AI accelerator cards by Nvidia, AMD, and Chinese chipmakers reached approximately 4 million units in China in 2025... Nvidia remained the market leader, shipping around 2.2 million cards and holding a 55% share.

key_facts.fact: Huawei led Chinese vendors with about 812,000 AI chips shipped, roughly half of all domestically branded shipments, followed by Alibaba's T-Head with 265,000 cards.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei Technologies emerged as the runaway leader among Chinese vendors, shipping around 812,000 AI chips, roughly half of all domestically branded shipments. Alibaba's chip design unit T-Head claimed second place, shipping approximately 265,000 cards.

key_facts.fact: Baidu's Kunlunxin and Cambricon each shipped around 116,000 cards, ranking jointly third among Chinese vendors.
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu's Kunlunxin and Cambricon each shipped around 116,000 cards, ranking them jointly third among Chinese vendors.

key_facts.fact: AMD held a modest 4% share with roughly 160,000 cards shipped in China.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD carved out a modest presence, shipping roughly 160,000 cards for a 4% share.

sources.title: Chinese chipmakers claim nearly half of local market as Nvidia's lead shrinks

stories.headline: Iranian Strike Damages AWS Data Center in Bahrain, Fourth Attack on Amazon Cloud Facilities

key_facts.fact: Amazon's cloud business in Bahrain was damaged by an Iranian strike on April 1, the fourth time AWS facilities in the Middle East have been hit.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's cloud business in Bahrain was damaged yet again on Wednesday due to an Iranian strike, the Financial Times reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The strike came one day after Iran's IRGC threatened to target American tech companies, with strikes to start on April 1 at 8 p.m. Iran time.
key_facts.excerpt: The strike comes only a day after Iran threatened to target American tech companies that it claimed were assisting 'US-Israeli terror operations,' with strikes to start on April 1.

key_facts.fact: Bahrain's Ministry of Interior confirmed civil defense was 'extinguishing a fire in a facility of a company as a result of the Iranian aggression' without naming the company.
key_facts.excerpt: Bahrain's Ministry of Interior said early Wednesday morning local time that the country's civil defense force was 'extinguishing a fire in a facility of a company as a result of the Iranian aggression,' without specifying which company it was.

key_facts.fact: The attacks mark the first time the data centers of an American tech giant have been targeted in military action.
key_facts.excerpt: The attacks marked the first time the data centers of an American tech giant were targeted in military action.

key_facts.fact: The British embassy in Saudi Arabia warned UK nationals to avoid U.S.-linked businesses, organisations, and facilities in the nation.
key_facts.excerpt: The British embassy in Saudi Arabia warned its nationals to avoid U.S.-linked businesses, organisations, and facilities in the nation, per the FT.

stories.headline: Amazon in Talks to Acquire Satellite Firm Globalstar for ~$9B to Rival SpaceX's Starlink

key_facts.fact: Amazon is in talks to buy satellite telecom group Globalstar as it builds its low-earth-orbit satellite business to compete with SpaceX's Starlink, according to the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon is in talks to buy satellite telecom group Globalstar as it ramps up efforts to build its own low-earth-orbit satellite business to rival SpaceX's Starlink, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: Globalstar shares surged 24% to $85 in extended trading, with a market cap of $8.81 billion as of last close.
key_facts.excerpt: Globalstar's shares, which have more than doubled in market value over the past year, surged 24% to $85 in extended trading following the report. The company had a market cap of $8.81 billion as of last close.

key_facts.fact: Apple's 20% stake in Globalstar, part of a $1.5 billion investment made in 2024, is a complicating factor requiring negotiations between Amazon and Apple.
key_facts.excerpt: One of the complicating factors is that Apple took a 20% stake in Globalstar in 2024, according to the FT, as part of a $1.5 billion investment to boost the company's constellation and ground infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's Leo satellite service has about 200 satellites in orbit so far and aims for a constellation of roughly 7,700 satellites, while Starlink has over 10,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon has launched about 200 satellites in low Earth orbit since last April, and it's aiming to roll out commercial service later this year. The company intends to build out a constellation of roughly 7,700 satellites.

key_facts.fact: Amazon asked the FCC for more time to meet a deadline requiring it to launch roughly 1,600 satellites by July 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon in January asked the Federal Communications Commission for more time to meet a deadline that requires it to launch roughly 1,600 satellites by July 2026.

stories.headline: NASA Launches Artemis II, First Crewed Moon Mission in 54 Years, With Four Astronauts

key_facts.fact: NASA's Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026, from Kennedy Space Center, sending four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon.
key_facts.excerpt: At 6:35 P.M. EDT, NASA's Artemis II mission blasted off from Kennedy Space Center. It's the second flight in the agency's moon-focused Artemis program and the first with humans onboard.

key_facts.fact: The crew — commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen — includes the first woman and person of color to go to the moon.
key_facts.excerpt: Onboard are commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and mission specialist (and rookie Canadian astronaut) Jeremy Hansen. It's the first time a woman, a person of color or a non-NASA astronaut will go to the moon.

key_facts.fact: The mission will loop around the moon's far side before returning to Earth; the crew will come within 4,000-6,000 miles of the lunar surface, the closest since Apollo 17 in 1972.
key_facts.excerpt: The Orion capsule will still be between 4,000 and 6,000 miles above the moon. Still, that's the closest any human has come to our nearest celestial companion since the last crewed landing during the Apollo 17 mission in 1972.

key_facts.fact: The 322-foot-tall SLS rocket attracted some 400,000 spectators to Florida's Space Coast, with millions more watching online.
key_facts.excerpt: The hulking Space Launch System (SLS) — a 322-foot-tall rocket flanked by boosters... The pyrotechnic performance attracted some 400,000 spectators to Florida's Space Coast, and millions more watched online.

key_facts.fact: The mission will test Orion spacecraft systems for long-duration crewed missions and potentially make the crew the farthest-flung humans in history.
key_facts.excerpt: The primary goal of Artemis II is to test the systems onboard the Orion spacecraft and ensure the capsule can support long-duration crewed missions... its trajectory will take it far beyond the lunar far side before it loops back toward home, a path that should make the Artemis II crew the farthest-flung humans in history.

stories.headline: Cognichip Raises $60M Series A to Build AI Models for Semiconductor Chip Design

key_facts.fact: Cognichip raised $60 million in a Series A led by Seligman Ventures, bringing total funding to $93 million since its 2024 founding.
key_facts.excerpt: The company emerged from stealth last year and said Wednesday that it had raised $60 million in new funding led by Seligman Ventures... Cognichip has now raised $93 million altogether since its founding in 2024.

key_facts.fact: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan will join Cognichip's board as a notable investor in the round.
key_facts.excerpt: with notable participation from Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who will be joining Cognichip's board.

key_facts.fact: Cognichip claims its technology can reduce chip development costs by more than 75% and cut timelines by more than half.

key_facts.fact: Cognichip competes with incumbent EDA players Synopsys and Cadence, and startups ChipAgents ($74M extended Series A) and Ricursive ($300M Series A).
key_facts.excerpt: Cognichip is competing against incumbent players like Synopsys and Cadence Design Systems, as well as well-funded startups like ChipAgents, which closed a $74 million extended Series A in February, and Ricursive, which raised a $300 million Series A round in January.

key_facts.fact: The startup uses its own model trained on chip design data rather than starting from a general-purpose LLM, and has developed methods for chipmakers to train on proprietary data without exposing it.

stories.headline: Raspberry Pi Raises Prices Up to $150 Citing 7x LPDDR4 Cost Increase, Launches 3GB Pi 4

key_facts.fact: Raspberry Pi implemented price increases across Pi 4 and Pi 5 variants with 4GB+ memory, citing a sevenfold increase in LPDDR4 DRAM prices over the past year.
key_facts.excerpt: the price of memory continues to rise, with a seven-fold increase over the last year in the price of the LPDDR4 DRAM used on Raspberry Pi 4 and 5.

key_facts.fact: Price increases range from $11.25 for 1GB Compute Modules to $150 for the Raspberry Pi 500+ unit, with the 16GB Pi 5 increasing by $100 to $299.99.
key_facts.excerpt: The price increases bring the 16GB Pi 5 up to $299.99.

key_facts.fact: A new 3GB Raspberry Pi 4 was introduced at $83.75 as a 'right-sized' option for users who don't need more memory.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we are implementing further price increases across parts of our product range, and are also introducing a new 3GB Raspberry Pi 4, priced at $83.75.

key_facts.fact: Eben Upton said memory prices 'won't remain at their current very high level indefinitely' and pledged to reverse increases when costs come down.
key_facts.excerpt: memory prices won't remain at their current very high level indefinitely; the circumstances in which we find ourselves are challenging, but in the future they will abate. When they do, we will reverse our price increases.

key_facts.fact: Jeff Geerling warned the hobbyist SBC market is 'dying or at least on life support' because LPDDR chips now account for the majority of board cost.
key_facts.excerpt: Unless the DRAM pricing situation changes radically, I think the hobbyist SBC market is dying — or at least on life support... LPDDR chips now account for the majority of board cost from the vendors I've checked with.

stories.headline: China's 7-Tonne Changying-8 Cargo Drone Completes Maiden Flight, Billed as World's Heaviest

key_facts.fact: China's Changying-8 (CY-8), a 7-tonne-class fixed-wing cargo drone developed by Norinco, completed its maiden flight at Zhengzhou airport on March 31, lasting about 30 minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: China Science reported that yet another large Chinese cargo drone, the Changying-8, had completed its maiden flight at Zhengzhou in China's Henan Province. The aircraft's first flight lasted for around 30 minutes.

key_facts.fact: The CY-8 has a maximum payload of 3.5 tonnes, an 18 cubic metre cargo compartment, and a range of over 3,000 kilometres.
key_facts.excerpt: The aircraft is China's first 7-tonne-class fixed-wing UAV, with a maximum payload capacity of 3.5 tonnes. The autonomous aircraft boasts an ultra-large cargo compartment with 18 cubic metres of volume... also comes with an advertised range of over 3,000 kilometres.

key_facts.fact: Chinese state media CCTV claimed it is the world's heaviest cargo drone to date, with a length of 17 metres and wingspan of 25 metres.
key_facts.excerpt: China's state-run CCTV claimed the CY-8 is the world's heaviest cargo drone to date. It has been dubbed the 'unmanned aerial heavy truck' in China. It comes with a length of 17 metres and a wingspan of 25 metres.

key_facts.fact: The drone has both civilian and military applications, including potential use for South China Sea island logistics and supply on the Tibetan Plateau.
key_facts.excerpt: Norinco says it can be used everywhere from islands to China's ultra-high Tibetan Plateau. SCMP notes, 'China is growing more reliant on drones in the South China Sea, where it has island disputes with several countries.'

key_facts.fact: The War Zone's Tyler Rogoway commented: 'The U.S. is falling way behind in uncrewed aerial logistics. I can't count how many of these China has in development now.'
key_facts.excerpt: Tyler Rogoway from The War Zone commented on the Changying-8 test flight, 'The U.S. is falling way behind in uncrewed aerial logistics. I can't count how many of these China has in development now.'

stories.headline: Delta Air Lines Picks Amazon Leo Over SpaceX Starlink for In-Flight WiFi on 500 Aircraft

key_facts.fact: Delta Air Lines chose Amazon's LEO satellite network over SpaceX's Starlink to power in-flight WiFi, with installations beginning on 500 aircraft starting in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Delta Air Lines has chosen Amazon's low-Earth-orbit satellite network to power its next-generation in-flight connectivity, bypassing the rapidly expanding Starlink ecosystem... Delta will begin installing Amazon's LEO satellite connectivity on 500 aircraft starting in 2028.

key_facts.fact: Delta CEO Ed Bastian said 'This agreement gives us the best, fastest and most cost-effective technology available to better connect the world.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Delta's future is global,' Bastian said. 'This agreement gives us the best, fastest and most cost-effective technology available to better connect the world today.'

key_facts.fact: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said Leo was designed to provide high-speed internet to billions of people without reliable connectivity.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We've designed Leo to provide high-speed internet to the billions of people on Earth without reliable connectivity, and this agreement with Delta is a great example of the impact and scale of the technology,' said Andy Jassy.

key_facts.fact: Other major carriers including United Airlines, IAG, and Lufthansa Group have selected Starlink, making Delta's Amazon choice a notable counter-move.
key_facts.excerpt: Several major carriers and airline groups — including United Airlines, IAG and Lufthansa Group — have already selected Starlink to upgrade onboard WiFi across their fleets.

key_facts.fact: Delta plans to integrate Amazon Leo with its Delta Sync digital platform, linking WiFi, seatback entertainment and personalized content through SkyMiles profiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Delta also plans to integrate the Amazon Leo network with its Delta Sync digital platform, which links inflight WiFi, seatback entertainment and personalised content through a passenger's SkyMiles profile.

key_facts.excerpt: Supermicro (SMCI) co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw and contractor Ting-Wei 'Willy' Sun both pleaded not guilty in a New York City courtroom on Wednesday for their alleged involvement in a scheme to illegally ship Nvidia-powered servers to China.

key_facts.fact: The case involves alleged smuggling of billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia-powered servers to China in violation of U.S. export controls.
